title: Backside encoder grating measures wafer distortion for EUV-free overlay
idea: Pattern a coarse 2D diffraction grating on the wafer backside at wafer start; encoder heads in the ArF-immersion scanner chuck read it to measure in-plane distortion under every exposure field, rather than at 30-80 alignment marks. The dense distortion map drives high-order field corrections so DUV LELE and spacer-patterned capacitor and bitline layers reach <1.5 nm overlay with no EUV.
why: Fact 4: overlay is what makes DUV multi-patterning expensive; good enough overlay lets DUV layers replace the 5-7 EUV layers, removing ~$200M scanners from the capex.

title: Printed-array wavefront retrieval tunes each DUV scanner lens for cells
idea: Treat the dense DRAM cell array printed in resist as a wavefront sensor: phase retrieval from through-focus scatterometry of the printed array extracts the scanner's actual aberrations at the cell pitch's diffraction orders. Feed them to the lens manipulators and co-optimize a per-scanner dipole/quadrupole source for the cell layer so ArF immersion holds process window at k1~0.27, with no EUV.
why: Fact 4: tighter single-exposure DUV pitch means one fewer multi-patterning pass on critical layers (one mask plus etch).

title: Spacer pitch-walk metrology fed forward enables EUV-free octuple patterning
idea: Measure mandrel CD and spacer thickness on every wafer (in-situ ellipsometry in the ALD tool plus integrated scatterometry), compute the pitch-walk populations self-aligned octuple patterning will produce, and feed forward per-wafer spacer-thickness and core-trim corrections for the next spacer generation. This makes SAOP from an ~80 nm ArF pitch down to ~10 nm lines manufacturable for bitlines and wordlines.
why: Fact 4: pitch walk is what kills SAOP; controlling it removes EUV from DRAM line/space layers, using ~$4M ALD/etch tools in place of $200M scanners.

title: Dose-reporting fluorescent resist verifies every DUV field before develop
idea: Add a photoacid-switchable fluorophore to ArF resist so post-exposure-bake fluorescence reports each field's absorbed dose; an in-track camera images the wafer before develop. Out-of-spec fields are reworked (strip and re-coat is cheap before develop), and the dose map feeds the scanner's dose correction for the next wafer.
why: Fact 4: DUV multi-patterning stacks 2-4 exposures per layer; catching dose errors pre-etch tightens CD uniformity ~30%, so EUV-free cell layers yield like single exposures.

title: Multibeam inspection plus beam-induced repair at each DUV layer
idea: Rather than drive DUV multi-patterning to near-zero defects, place a 100+-beam SEM after each critical develop/hardmask etch to find bridges and missing features, then fix them at the same station with gas-assisted electron-beam-induced etch or deposition. Lay out cell layers so likely defects sit on sacrificial hardmask and are repaired before pattern transfer.
why: Fact 4: lets cheaper EUV-free patterning flows with higher raw defect density reach EUV-class yields, provided ~10-100 repairs per wafer fit the cycle time.

title: Spectroscopic resist fingerprinting qualifies second-source DUV photoresists in weeks
idea: Build a fingerprint panel (solution NMR, LC-MS of the photoacid generator, dissolution-rate monitor, and a contrast-curve test chip) that captures an ArF resist's lithographic behavior quantitatively. Qualify domestic or non-Japanese ArF resists and rinses by matching the incumbent's fingerprint within tolerance, cutting qualification from 12-18 months to weeks.
why: Scarce resources and U.S. manufacturability: ArF resists are a >80% Japanese chokepoint; dual-sourcing protects DUV-only DRAM lines.

title: Sense-amp charge-sharing maps turn every die into full-wafer CD metrology
idea: Add a test mode in which each sense amplifier measures its bitline and cell capacitance by charge sharing against a reference, producing a per-column map of electrical CD (bitline width, contact size, capacitor area) on every die at wafer sort. Feed these 100%-sampled maps lot-to-lot to the DUV scanners and etchers, replacing much CD-SEM sampling and holding multi-patterned cell layers tight enough to stay EUV-free.
why: Fact 4: replaces ~30-50% of CD-SEM capex with ~1000x more data points; tighter CD uniformity extends DUV-only scaling by about a node.

title: On-product tolerance experiments downgrade layers from ArF to KrF/i-line
idea: Deliberately perturb each layer's CD, focus and overlay on a few product wafers (a per-field DOE) and measure the electrical yield response, giving a measured tolerance for every layer. Layers with loose true tolerance move from ArF immersion to KrF or i-line steppers, with layout tweaks (wider landing pads) where needed; nothing uses EUV.
why: Fact 4: 20-30% of DRAM layers may be over-served by ArF; KrF/i-line tools cost 5-20x less, cutting litho capex ~15%.

title: Angle-resolved Faraday metrology enables tilted-implant shadow pitch splitting
idea: Build an in-chamber angle-resolved ion detector (Faraday cups behind a micro-collimator array) that measures beam angular spread to ~0.05 degrees. With angle known that precisely, use tilted implants or ion-beam etches that shadow off DUV-printed mandrels to modify only one sidewall's hardmask, splitting pitch 2x without another lithography step or EUV.
why: Fact 4: each shadow step replaces a litho pass (mask plus scanner time); on bitline/contact layers it saves 1-2 DUV exposures.

title: Terahertz emission junction mapping lets fabs merge periphery implant masks
idea: Scan a femtosecond laser over the wafer and record the terahertz emission whose amplitude and polarity encode built-in junction field and depth, giving a non-contact, 100%-coverage junction map. With every die's junctions verified, merge periphery threshold-adjust implants into fewer masks by implanting through screen layers whose local thickness comes from existing gate-stack patterns, trimming dose per lot from the terahertz data; all masks stay KrF/ArF, no EUV.
why: Facts 7 and 4: periphery uses ~10-15 implant masks; cutting 3-4 saves mask, litho and strip steps (~3-5% wafer cost).

title: Slow-positron vacancy profiling enables low-temperature capacitor dielectric crystallization
idea: A wafer-scale slow-positron beam (moderated isotope source) measures depth-resolved oxygen-vacancy and open-volume concentration in ZrO2/HfO2 capacitor dielectrics. Using it as the feedback signal, develop a plasma-oxidation plus ~400 C crystallization that reaches the high-k phase with low vacancy density, replacing a hot anneal and its furnace capacity, in an EUV-free capacitor module.
why: Facts 1 and 4: lower thermal budget, fewer furnace tools, and vacancy-controlled leakage that lets k rise without a leakage penalty, relieving the aspect-ratio wall.

title: In-reactor X-ray diffraction locks Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy for 3D DRAM
idea: Mount fast in-situ high-resolution XRD on the epi reactor to measure each layer's Ge fraction and thickness as it grows, adjusting precursor flows layer by layer. Drift-free 100-200-layer Si/SiGe stacks then let one set of DUV-patterned hole and slit masks serve all tiers of a 3D DRAM, with no EUV layer.
why: Fact 2: superlattice drift limits tier count; in-situ control could allow 2-3x more tiers, each costing deposition rather than lithography.

title: Bevel metrology shrinks edge exclusion, adding die without new lithography
idea: An edge-profile instrument (multi-angle laser triangulation plus spectral imaging of the bevel) measures film termination, edge bead and bevel deposits on every wafer. With precise edge knowledge, tune edge-bead removal and bevel etch per wafer to cut edge exclusion from ~3 mm to ~1 mm, and add partial-field die exposures on the DUV scanner.
why: Capital per bit: +3-4% gross die per wafer at near-zero capex; at 100k wafer-starts/month that equals adding ~3-4k wafers/month of capacity, EUV-free.

title: Laser-pulse row-hammer emulator screens isolation quality mid-process
idea: Instead of electrically hammering finished chips, a focused pulsed laser injects carriers near a wordline on a partially processed array test structure, and charge loss in neighbouring cells is read through a test sense path: a seconds-long proxy for hammer susceptibility right after isolation and buried-wordline formation. With hammer margin measured per lot, the cell flow drops one deep channel-stop implant mask (DUV, no EUV) and reinstates it only for failing lots.
why: Fact 9: saves a mask (~1-2% wafer cost) and replaces worst-case isolation margin with measured margin.

title: Automated plasma-FIB tomography closes DRAM failure-analysis loops within hours
idea: A robotic plasma-FIB-SEM cell takes failing-bit addresses straight from wafer test, auto-slices 3D volumes around ~50 failing cells per day and classifies root causes, replacing week-long manual TEM failure analysis. Plan the yield ramp of a DUV-only (no EUV) fab, whose extra multi-patterning layers multiply failure modes, around daily FA loops.
why: Fact 4: an idle ramping fab burns ~$10M/day of depreciation; halving ramp time from ~12 to ~6 months saves billions.

title: Per-layer X-ray laminography lets HBM stacks be reworked before molding
idea: In-line 3D X-ray laminography images every microbump or hybrid-bond joint after each die is placed in an 8-16-high HBM stack, catching non-wets and voids; a failing top die is thermally released and replaced before the next die goes on. The stacking flow becomes measure-each-layer and rework-in-place, entirely EUV-free.
why: Fact 6: stack yield losses of 20-30% fall toward 5-10%, cutting HBM wafer area per good bit by up to ~20%.

title: Step-level energy submetering lets fabs shift heavy steps to cheap power
idea: Meter every tool, pump and abatement unit against lot-step IDs to build a measured energy-per-step ledger, then schedule buffer-tolerant heavy steps (furnace batches, epi, abatement regeneration) into low-price, high-renewable hours, sizing WIP buffers from the ledger. With no EUV scanners (each ~1 MW, always on) in the flow, a larger share of load becomes shiftable.
why: Energy chokepoint: 10-20% lower fab energy cost and a grid-friendly load profile that eases U.S. siting.

title: Effluent-sensed rinse endpoints cut ultrapure water per wafer
idea: Put fast conductivity, TOC and particle sensors on every wet-bench rinse drain and end each rinse when the effluent reaches baseline instead of after a fixed time; route clean late-rinse water back to the UPW loop when the sensors confirm quality. Pairs with an EUV-free flow whose extra multi-patterning cleans make rinse water a larger share of demand.
why: Water and throughput: 30-40% less rinse water and shorter wet-bench cycles, so fewer benches.

title: Diffraction-locked resist reflow shrinks DUV contact holes uniformly
idea: During a thermal reflow bake of ArF-printed holes, a diffraction monitor reads the hole array's first-order efficiency, which tracks hole diameter, and stops each zone of a segmented hotplate at the target CD. Old, poorly controlled resist reflow becomes a precise sub-resolution shrink, so DUV LELE sets the pitch and measured reflow sets the ~20 nm CD of contact and capacitor holes, with no EUV.
why: Fact 4: replaces an EUV hole layer, or an extra shrink/etch pass, with a bake step on existing tracks.

title: Eddy-current tomography in the pad merges two-step CMP into one
idea: A multi-frequency eddy-current sensor array in the polishing pad images remaining metal and dishing under the wafer during polishing, and a zone-pressure carrier uses that image to finish both bulk removal and barrier clearing on one platen. Buried-wordline and bitline CMP become a single controlled step with less overpolish, and the flatter topography widens the depth-of-focus budget for EUV-free multi-patterning.
why: Fact 4: ~10% lower CMP capex and consumables, plus focus margin that helps DUV hold critical layers.

title: IR interferometric thickness mapping enables 20 um HBM dies with tiny TSVs
idea: Measure the total thickness variation of every thinning wafer in 2D at ~100 um pitch with backside IR low-coherence interferometry during grinding, adjusting chuck tilt and zones in real time. Uniform thinning to ~20 um lets TSV diameter shrink from ~5 um to ~2 um at the same aspect ratio, still patterned by i-line/KrF with no EUV.
why: Fact 6: TSV plus keep-out area drops ~4x, and thinner dies allow 16-24-high stacks within the same height.
